ola-ro-05-edu.alt: La petrecerea de Crăciun pentru angajați, VAT-ul se recuperează.
ola-ro-05-edu.title: Două mese de Crăciun, două tratamente diferite
ola-ro-05-edu.caption_full:
Decembrie aduce două mese care arată la fel pe extrasul de cont și se tratează complet diferit. Masa de Crăciun a echipei: VAT-ul se cere înapoi, iar directorii pot sta la aceeași masă cu angajații, fără să se schimbe nimic. Masa cu un client sau cu un partener de afaceri: VAT-ul nu se recuperează, oricât de mult ar semăna cu munca. Nici masa la care stau numai directorii nu dă drept de recuperare. Iar dacă la eveniment vin și angajați și invitați din afară, se recuperează numai partea angajaților. Două condiții fără care nimic din toate acestea nu se aplică: firma trebuie să fie înregistrată în VAT și să ceară suma prin VAT Return, iar tu trebuie să ai factura cu VAT, nu doar bonul de card.

Salvează postarea înainte să rezervi masa.

ola-ro-07-edu.alt: De la 1 decembrie, benzină până la 1400cc: 16p pe milă.
ola-ro-07-edu.title: Baremul pe milă pentru mașina firmei se schimbă
ola-ro-07-edu.caption_full:
Un om din firma ta face 400 de mile cu mașina companiei în decembrie, o benzină de 1.4. La 16p pe milă îi dai 64 de lire pentru combustibil și nu apare nici venit impozabil, nici National Insurance. Asta fac baremele acestea. De la 1 decembrie 2026, benzină: 16p până la 1400cc, 19p între 1401 și 2000cc, 29p peste 2000cc. Diesel: 16p până la 1600cc, 18p între 1601 și 2000cc, 25p peste 2000cc. LPG: 11p, 13p și 20p pe aceleași trepte. Complet electric: 7p la încărcare acasă, 15p la încărcare publică. Dacă plătești mai mult decât baremul și nu poți arăta un cost real mai mare pe milă, diferența devine venit impozabil. Baremul vechi mai poate fi folosit încă o lună după 1 decembrie 2026. Două lucruri pe care tabelul nu le acoperă: camionetele, care nu au barem aici, și un motor în afara treptelor de mai sus, pentru care rămâne doar costul tău real pe milă, dovedit cu documente. Iar cine e self-employed nu folosește baremul acesta niciodată.

Salvează lista, o să-ți trebuiască la următoarea rambursare.

bham-06-edu.alt: Gifts to one customer add up: £50 in any 12 months, then VAT is due.
bham-06-edu.title: The 50 pound gift rule people get wrong every Christmas
bham-06-edu.caption_full:
It is the season for dropping something off with a good customer, so here is the line that catches people. If you are VAT registered, you can give one customer gifts costing up to 50 pounds in total, excluding VAT, in any 12-month period, and there is no VAT for you to account for. The trap is the word total. It is not 50 pounds per gift. Three hampers at 30 pounds each to the same customer passes it, and VAT is then due on the cost of all of them, not just the amount over 50. bham-07-edu.caption_full:

en-06-edu.alt: Over £50,000 profit, your company is not suddenly all taxed at 25%.
en-06-edu.title: No, 25% does not land on your whole profit
en-06-edu.caption_full:
A lot of directors believe that the moment profits pass £50,000, the whole lot is taxed at 25%. They are usually relieved to find out otherwise. Profits of £50,000 or less are charged at 19%, the small profits rate. Profits over £250,000 are charged at the main rate of 25%. Between the two, Marginal Relief tapers the rate up from one to the other, so the effective rate climbs gradually rather than falling off a cliff at £50,001. Two groups do not get it: companies that are not resident in the UK, and close investment-holding companies. And if you hold several companies, those £50,000 and £250,000 limits get divided between them, which catches directors out far more often than the rates themselves do.

Save this before you decide whether to take the extra work on.

en-07-edu.alt: If your company pays you interest on a loan, it must hold back 20%.
en-07-edu.title: Your company pays you interest? Hold back 20%
en-07-edu.caption_full:
This one catches a particular sort of company, and if it is not yours you can stop reading with a clear conscience. If your company borrowed money from you, or from a family member, and pays interest on that loan, it cannot simply hand over the full amount. It has to hold back 20% basic rate Income Tax, pay that over to HMRC, and report it on a form called CT61 - within 14 days of the end of each return period. For the period ending 31 December 2026, that means 14 January 2027. Nothing in the payroll or VAT cycle prompts you, which is why this is the deadline owner-managed companies miss most. You then show the gross interest and the tax credit on your own return. And if the interest goes to a UK bank, or to another UK company, or to a charity or an approved pension fund, none of it applies - which is why most companies never meet the form at all.

Save this if your company pays interest to a person rather than a bank.

You then show the gross interest and the tax credit on your own return. And if the interest goes to a UK bank, or to another UK company, or to a charity or an approved pension fund, none of it applies - which is why most companies never meet the form at all.

en-08-joke.alt: Whichever comes out first is the business one.
en-08-joke.title: One wallet, two cards, and a coin toss at the till
en-08-joke.caption_full:
Nobody sets out to mix the two. It happens because the nearest card wins, and because at half past four with the van running you are not thinking about who owns the coffee. Then the year ends and somebody goes down a bank statement line by line, in the evening, deciding which sandwich was work. One card for the business, and only the business, takes that whole job away. It also means that when you finally look at what the business spent, you are looking at the business, and not at a fortnight of family shopping in March.

en-09-joke.alt: Their accounts team has its own calendar.
en-09-joke.title: Your invoice says 30 days. Their calendar disagrees
en-09-joke.caption_full:
Thirty days, it says on the invoice. Thirty days from when, exactly, turns out to be a matter of interpretation at their end. This is the part of running a business that nobody warns you about: you can be busy, profitable on paper, and still unable to pay your own bills, because the money that proves you are profitable is sitting in somebody else's account. Knowing what is owed to you, and how old each of it is, is not admin. It is the difference between a good year and a frightening one.

en-10-quote.alt: It is not enough to be industrious; so are the ants. What are you industrious about?
en-10-quote.title: Busy is easy. Busy at what is the real question
en-10-quote.caption_full:
Thoreau was not against hard work. He was against hard work that nobody has asked the purpose of. Busy is easy. Busy is the default setting of anybody running their own business - the day fills itself, and at the end of it you have certainly moved, without having necessarily moved forward. The question underneath is a business question as much as a philosophical one: of everything you did today, how much of it was the work, and how much of it was motion? Worth a minute of a dark evening.
